geometry_edits.rationale: Recast the dominant mass as split wings to create an active ground seam and a clear public void while preserving a single dominant body.
Orient the split to better address the access edge and avoid a sealed frontage.
Enlarge the void so it reads as usable public space rather than decorative subtraction.
Retain a bridging connection to preserve hierarchy and continuity in the section.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the single cantilever block with a split-wing logic to produce a clearer active ground threshold and a more legible public void toward the access edge.
Set the split axis so the mass opens across the frontage direction and creates a more explicit street-facing gap.
Increase separation to establish a meaningful void rather than a shallow nick.
Keep a connecting upper link so the form remains one coherent dominant gesture after the split.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent object in all four views, but it reads as a generic compact block with a small terrace/cut rather than a clearly programed neighborhood-building mass. The dominant gesture is readable, yet the open-space figure is too shallow and not legibly public; the blue frontage edge is met with a sealed or ambiguous ground response instead of a strong entry seam, canopy, court, or undercut. The stepped/terraced roof logic is present but feels incidental rather than capacity-bearing or sectionally programmatic. Overall it is not visually contradictory, but it does not yet satisfy the semantic contract of an active neighborhood living mass with one clear public void and an aligned street threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller and more vertical than the candidate; its public-ground logic is weakly applicable to neighborhood living and should not be copied as a tower typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact tower/superblock reads as a single dominant mass with a clear tapered/stepped profile and strong silhouette hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office tower typology is not the same as a low-rise neighborhood building; use only the principle of a unified profile, not the program scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A continuous single-volume mass can gain legibility through controlled tapering and a coherent setback crown.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is closer in program and ground relationship, but the candidate lacks the same clarity of public entry and active frontage.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low horizontal commercial massing with an explicit canopy/threshold and adjacent vertical sign element reinforces active street edge.

warnings: Primary road frontage/access edge appears to be the thick blue segment; the candidate does not clearly open toward it.
Parcel containment appears broadly respected, but the plan response is too box-like and under-articulated.
No visible sectional program move (entry bridge/court/active ground) is strong enough to carry the neighborhood-living brief.
